lines.text: This hexagon is cut into twenty-four little triangles. But that's not the whole story!
lines.caption: This hexagon is cut into twenty-four little triangles. But that's not the whole story!

lines.text: Bigger triangles are hiding in it too. Some of them are sneaky.
lines.caption: Bigger triangles are hiding in it too. Some of them are sneaky.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's hunt down every triangle.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's hunt down every triangle.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A regular hexagon has side length two.
lines.caption: A regular hexagon has side length two.

lines.text: It's cut into twenty-four small equilateral triangles.
lines.caption: It's cut into twenty-four small equilateral triangles.

lines.text: How many triangles of any size are in the figure?
lines.caption: How many triangles of any size are in the figure?

lines.text: Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices.

lines.text: Each little triangle has side one. Two small edges make a hexagon side.
lines.caption: Each little triangle has side one. Two small edges make a hexagon side.

lines.text: We count triangles of every size, as long as their edges are drawn lines.
lines.caption: We count triangles of every size, as long as their edges are drawn lines.

lines.text: And watch the direction. Some triangles point up, and some point down.
lines.caption: And watch the direction. Some triangles point up, and some point down.

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's count one size at a time.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's count one size at a time.

lines.text: Side one is easy. Those are the twenty-four little triangles we were given.
lines.caption: Side one is easy. Those are the twenty-four little triangles we were given.

lines.text: Side two is made of four small triangles.
lines.caption: Side two is made of four small triangles.

lines.text: Six of them fit around the center, like slices of a pizza.
lines.caption: Six of them fit around the center, like slices of a pizza.

lines.text: Each slice has a corner right at the center.
lines.caption: Each slice has a corner right at the center.

lines.text: But here's a sneaky one. None of its corners is at the center.
lines.caption: But here's a sneaky one. None of its corners is at the center.

lines.text: The center sits in the middle of one of its sides.
lines.caption: The center sits in the middle of one of its sides.

lines.text: There are six of these too, each pointing to the middle of a hexagon side.
lines.caption: There are six of these too, each pointing to the middle of a hexagon side.

lines.text: So side two gives six plus six, twelve triangles.
lines.caption: So side two gives six plus six, twelve triangles.

lines.text: What about side three? Look at the middle of each side of the hexagon.
lines.caption: What about side three? Look at the middle of each side of the hexagon.

lines.text: Join every other middle, and you get one big triangle pointing up.
lines.caption: Join every other middle, and you get one big triangle pointing up.

lines.text: Join the other three, and you get one pointing down. That's two.
lines.caption: Join the other three, and you get one pointing down. That's two.

lines.text: Side four won't fit. Its bottom edge would need one of the long lines through the middle.
lines.caption: Side four won't fit. Its bottom edge would need one of the long lines through the middle.

lines.text: But only two rows fit above or below that line.
lines.caption: But only two rows fit above or below that line.

lines.text: Twenty-four plus twelve plus two is thirty-eight. That's Choice E!
lines.caption: Twenty-four plus twelve plus two is thirty-eight. That's Choice E!

lines.text: Time for a clever shortcut. Count only the triangles that point up.
lines.caption: Time for a clever shortcut. Count only the triangles that point up.

lines.text: Twelve of the small ones point up.
lines.caption: Twelve of the small ones point up.

lines.text: Six of the side-two triangles point up, and one of the big ones.
lines.caption: Six of the side-two triangles point up, and one of the big ones.

lines.text: That's twelve plus six plus one, nineteen.
lines.caption: That's twelve plus six plus one, nineteen.

lines.text: Now turn the hexagon upside down. It looks the same, but every up triangle now points down!
lines.caption: Now turn the hexagon upside down. It looks the same, but every up triangle now points down!

lines.text: So there are nineteen pointing down too. Two times nineteen is thirty-eight.
lines.caption: So there are nineteen pointing down too. Two times nineteen is thirty-eight.

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the shape looks the same upside down.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the shape looks the same upside down.

lines.text: Now the traps. Choice A, twenty-four, counts only the little triangles.
lines.caption: Now the traps. Choice A, twenty-four, counts only the little triangles.

lines.text: Choice B, thirty, is what you'd get if you found only the six pizza slices of side two.
lines.caption: Choice B, thirty, is what you'd get if you found only the six pizza slices of side two.

lines.text: Choice C, thirty-two, counts side-two triangles in only one direction.
lines.caption: Choice C, thirty-two, counts side-two triangles in only one direction.

lines.text: Choice D, thirty-six, forgets the two big triangles that stretch across the hexagon.
lines.caption: Choice D, thirty-six, forgets the two big triangles that stretch across the hexagon.

lines.text: Count every size, in both directions, and you get thirty-eight.
lines.caption: Count every size, in both directions, and you get thirty-eight.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? This big triangle has side four. It's cut into sixteen small triangles.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? This big triangle has side four. It's cut into sixteen small triangles.

lines.text: How many triangles of any size are in it?
lines.caption: How many triangles of any size are in it?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Side one: the sixteen small ones.
lines.caption: Let's check. Side one: the sixteen small ones.

lines.text: Side two: six point up. And don't miss the sneaky one in the middle, pointing down. That's seven.
lines.caption: Side two: six point up. And don't miss the sneaky one in the middle, pointing down. That's seven.

lines.text: Side three: three of them, one in each corner.
lines.caption: Side three: three of them, one in each corner.

lines.text: Side four: the whole triangle.
lines.caption: Side four: the whole triangle.

lines.text: Sixteen plus seven plus three plus one is twenty-seven!
lines.caption: Sixteen plus seven plus three plus one is twenty-seven!

lines.text: If you got twenty-seven, outstanding hunting!
lines.caption: If you got twenty-seven, outstanding hunting!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Count the triangles one size at a time, and check both directions, up and down.
lines.caption: Count the triangles one size at a time, and check both directions, up and down.

lines.text: If the shape looks the same upside down, count one direction and double it.
lines.caption: If the shape looks the same upside down, count one direction and double it.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep hunting, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep hunting, and I'll see you next time!
